newsitem.title: UK: LME copper nervously softer ahead of stocks data.
newsitem.headline: LME copper nervously softer ahead of stocks data.

text.p: LME copper nervously oscillated in a narrow band on Thursday afternoon, ending marginally softer ahead of stocks data on Friday.
"Copper seems to have run out of steam," said analyst William Adams of broker Rudolf Wolff, adding that producer forward selling and buying of puts had been seen.
Three months copper ended the afternoon kerb $12 weaker at $2,328 per tonne after earlier nudging the upside above $2,350.
Traders would closely watch stocks data on Friday, the first since the February prompt date. LME inventories were expected to see a modest fall, traders said.
Any stocks rise, though, could knock copper's stance at 8-1/2 month highs.
"I don't really trust the market up here. Fundamentally I find these levels as hard to justify," Adams said.
If prices move lower, it could try to fill a chart gap at $2,290-$2,315, he added.
Most of the other metals ended weaker, but aluminium showed independence and finished $3 firmer at $1,607.
"Ally has had a good pull back from $1,650 to $1,534 and should be ready to move higher now," Adams said.
Zinc shed $14 to $1,216 after failing for the second day to break above $1,234/5.
It was looking overbought and may be due for a correction. If it fell below $1,200, support should emerge at $1,190 and $1,150.
Nickel, which has also had a good run recently, lost $60 to finish at $7,850.
Tin declined $45 to $6,020 and lead lost $3 to $667.
Alloy was up slightly at $1,532/5 versus $1,530.
